obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 1. No accounts, names or free-text input for children. Ever.

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 2. When a kit's `logging_enabled` is false, the server stores nothing about that kit's activity. The `p6-nolog-invariant` test must never be skipped, weakened or deleted.

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 3. Class and kit identity come from the session, never from a request body.

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 4. Plain kit codes, join codes and tokens are never stored or logged. IP addresses are never stored or logged.

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 5. No request from the browser to any origin but our own. No third-party scripts, fonts, analytics or embeds. The one exception is the embedded YouTube player's origins, on pages that show a module video ([ADR 0025](docs/adr/0025-youtube-embedded-module-video.md)).

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 7. Do not write teaching content for the kit. Use the `demo` kit for development. Real content comes from Given.

obligations.section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
obligations.text: 8. The decisions in `docs/adr/` stand. If one looks wrong, file a `decision` bead and stop.
- Work one bead at a time, lowest phase and highest priority first.
- **Never start a bead labelled `human`.** If one blocks you, say so and stop, or pick other ready work.
- A bead is done when every acceptance criterion is met, tests pass locally and in CI, and the change is merged. Not before.
- Found something out of scope? `bd create "..." -t task -p 2 --deps discovered-from:<current-id>` and carry on. Do not widen the current bead.

- Run a separate planloop for each major implementation. That means work in one of planloop's risk domains (it would start on the escalated track), a new mechanism, or a change to a migration, the event catalog, the content format or the authorization matrix.
- An approved plan is not authorization to implement. Implementation waits for Mike's go-ahead.
3. Implement with tests. Every new route goes into the authorization matrix test.
4. Run `pnpm lint && pnpm check && pnpm test && pnpm e2e`.
5. Commit with the bead ID in the message. Merge once CI is green; staging deploys itself.

The platform serves any kit. A kit is a `products` row (slug, name, code prefix) and a `content/<slug>/` folder. First product: the mechanical arm, slug `arm`, prefix `ARM`. Both are placeholders until the team names the kit; changing them before codes are printed is a one-line change.
Server code is split into `auth`, `codes`, `content`, `events`, `analytics` modules that talk through their `index.ts`.
PostgreSQL 16. Drizzle for typed queries. Migrations are SQL files, forward-only, run on deploy. Analytics is SQL views in the same database.
- Migrations stay compatible with the previous app version, so rollback to the previous image works (ARCHITECTURE.md section 10; p10-cd jade-kn0 description).

Adults: email + password, argon2id, server-side sessions. Signup requires a valid unused kit code or a staff invite. Password reset is a staff action. Students: class join code plus kit selection, yielding a device-session cookie bound to class and kit. No accounts for children.
`logging_enabled` per kit per class, default off, switched on by an adult who confirms consent. Off means zero activity stored server-side. A required test enforces this.
`PREFIX-XXXX-XXXX-C`, Crockford Base32, CSPRNG, check character. Stored as HMAC-SHA256 under a server-side pepper. Plain codes exist only on print and in an offline CSV.

- Each card's QR opens `/redeem?code=...` (p2-code-cli jade-99j description), so the plain code also travels in a URL, into the adult device's browser history and the request line. The Decision's "Plain codes exist only on print and in an offline CSV" does not cover this. The conflict is open; this ADR does not settle it, and the threat model written by p0-threat (jade-okb) records it.
- Losing the pepper invalidates every printed code (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6).
No analytics, fonts, CDNs, embeds or error trackers that load in the user's browser. CSP enforces it and an e2e test asserts it.
Staging exists before feature work and is deployed on every merge to main. Production receives the image that passed staging.
Decided (Mike, 2026-11-14): global throttle for now; per-IP signup limit kept as a toggle (config flag, off by default) for later. Redeem stays per account.

- The global throttle is shared by everyone, so anyone submitting wrong codes can delay legitimate redemption and signup for everyone. The threat model written by p0-threat (jade-okb) records this lockout risk.
- The sources do not say how the per-account redeem limit and the global throttle interact.
Production actions stay human.
- Everything else in ADR 0013 stays: no third-party scripts, fonts, analytics, error trackers or other embeds. No page without a module video makes any request to another origin.
Names are binding, exact column types may be adjusted if a test shows a reason.
Conventions: `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` unless stated, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`, all timestamps `timestamptz`, text enums as `text` with a `check`.

create table products (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  slug        text not null unique,            -- 'arm' (placeholder), matches content/<slug>/
  name        text not null,
  code_prefix text not null unique check (code_prefix ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'),
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table code_batches (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  product_id  uuid not null references products(id),
  label       text not null,                   -- 'pilot1-v1'
  created_by  uuid references users(id),
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (product_id, label)
);

create table kits (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),   -- the anonymous kit ID; lifelong
  product_id  uuid not null references products(id),
  batch_id    uuid not null references code_batches(id),
  serial      int  not null,                   -- number printed on the kit label within its batch
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (batch_id, serial)
);

create table kit_codes (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  kit_id        uuid not null references kits(id),
  code_hmac     bytea not null unique,         -- HMAC-SHA256(pepper, normalised code). Never the code.
  entitlements  text[] not null default '{core}',
  status        text not null default 'unused' check (status in ('unused','redeemed','revoked')),
  redeemed_by   uuid references users(id),
  redeemed_at   timestamptz,
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table users (
  id             uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  email          citext not null unique,
  password_hash  text not null,                -- argon2id
  display_name   text,
  role           text not null default 'adult' check (role in ('adult','staff')),
  created_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
  disabled_at    timestamptz
);

create table auth_sessions (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id       uuid not null references users(id) on delete cascade,
  token_hash    bytea not null unique,         -- sha256 of a 256-bit random token
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_seen_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  expires_at    timestamptz not null
);

create table invites (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  token_hash   bytea not null unique,
  role         text not null default 'adult',
  created_by   uuid not null references users(id),
  expires_at   timestamptz not null,
  accepted_by  uuid references users(id),
  accepted_at  timestamptz
);

create table classes (
  id             uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  owner_id       uuid not null references users(id),
  name           text not null,
  kind           text not null check (kind in ('classroom','camp','home')),
  pilot_label    text,                          -- 'pilot-1', 'pilot-2'; used by analytics filters
  join_code_hash bytea,                         -- set while a session is open
  join_open      boolean not null default false,
  ended_at       timestamptz,                   -- retention clock starts here
  created_at     timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table class_kits (
  class_id              uuid not null references classes(id) on delete cascade,
  kit_id                uuid not null references kits(id),
  display_number        int  not null,          -- 'Kit 07' as shown to students
  logging_enabled       boolean not null default false,
  consent_confirmed_by  uuid references users(id),
  consent_confirmed_at  timestamptz,
  active                boolean not null default true,
  primary key (class_id, kit_id),
  unique (class_id, display_number)
);

create table device_sessions (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  class_id      uuid not null,
  kit_id        uuid not null,
  token_hash    bytea not null unique,
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_seen_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  revoked_at    timestamptz,
  foreign key (class_id, kit_id) references class_kits(class_id, kit_id) on delete cascade
);

create table audit_log (
  id          bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  at          timestamptz not null default now(),
  actor_id    uuid references users(id),
  action      text not null,                    -- 'code.redeem', 'kit.logging_on', 'kit.delete_data', ...
  subject     jsonb not null                    -- ids and counts only; never codes, tokens or note text
);
create unique index one_live_code_per_kit on kit_codes(kit_id) where status <> 'revoked';
create unique index kit_in_one_active_class on class_kits(kit_id) where active;
Adult email is the only personal information in the system.

Format `ARM-7KQ4-XM2H-9`: a 3-letter product prefix (placeholder `ARM` until the kit is named), 8 random Crockford Base32 characters, 1 check character. Crockford drops I, L, O and U, so codes survive being read aloud by a child.

- 8 Base32 characters are 40 bits, about 1.1 trillion combinations. That defeats online guessing behind a rate limit. It does **not** defeat offline brute force of a leaked table of plain hashes, which is why the database stores `HMAC-SHA256(pepper, code)` with a server-side secret, not `SHA-256(code)`.
- The plain code exists in two places only: the printed card and the packing CSV kept offline.
- A code maps to a `kit_id`. The kit keeps that ID for life, across pilots and classes, so a reused kit has one history.
- Redemption is single-use, transactional and audited. Staff can revoke and reissue.
- Losing the pepper invalidates every printed code. Its backup procedure is a launch task (`p10-secrets`).
| Guessing kit codes online | Rate limit per account, lockout, check character rejects most typos before the server |
| Brute-forcing a leaked code table | HMAC with server-side pepper |
| Student reaching adult or staff pages | Route-group authorization matrix, 404 not 403 |
| IP addresses as hidden identifiers | Not logged by Caddy or the app; used in memory for rate limiting only |
- **Releases:** build image, run forward-only migrations, start, health-check, switch. Rollback is the previous image. Migrations stay compatible with the previous app version.

obligations.section: 7. Open until the human beads close
obligations.text: - TM-4 (open): Scanning a code card's QR leaves the plain kit code in the adult device's browser history (`/redeem?code=...`, p2-code-cli jade-99j). No bead addresses it, and only single-use redemption (jade-7if) limits its value. Whether p2-redeem should keep the code out of the URL after the scan, or this is accepted, is not decided. ADR 0011 records the same conflict with its statement that plain codes exist only on print and in an offline CSV.

obligations.section: 7. Open until the human beads close
obligations.text: - TM-5 (open): Joining writes a `device_sessions` row (which has a `last_seen_at` column, DATA-MODEL.md section 3) for a kit with logging off. Whether that is stored activity under CLAUDE.md rule 2 ("the server stores nothing about that kit's activity") is not decided; the no-log invariant of p6-nolog-invariant (jade-hhp) lists events, kit_progress, notes and quiz tables only. This document records the fact; it does not answer the question.
- **Rate-limit counters.** IP addresses are used in memory only and never written to disk (p9-ratelimit jade-6cq; ADR 0020). Where the other counters live is not decided (section 4, `RL_MEM`).

- **Kits and kit codes.** A kit keeps its id for life (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6); staff can revoke and reissue a code, keeping the kit id (p2-staff-codes jade-pe9), and a revoked code row stays with status `revoked` (DATA-MODEL.md section 1). No source gives `kits` or `kit_codes` a deletion rule.

- **Audit log.** `audit_log` holds actor ids and ids and counts only, never codes, tokens or note text (DATA-MODEL.md section 3); kit deletion adds a row to it (jade-l13). No source gives it a retention or deletion rule.

- **Printed cards and packing CSV.** The CLI warns that the files are the only copy (jade-99j), and the CSV is stored offline (p10-codes jade-t17). No source says when they are destroyed; a used code is spent by single-use redemption (jade-7if).

- **Files are immutable once merged.** A merged file is never edited, renamed, reordered or
  removed. There is no down migration and no way to reapply a file: a mistake is corrected by a
  new migration.

- **`manifest.json` is the lock.** It lists every file's name and SHA-256 in order. The runner
  refuses files that do not match it, and stops with `MIGRATION_HISTORY_MISMATCH`, applying
  nothing, when an applied file's name or hash differs from the ledger (`schema_migrations`).
  The manifest is also what the app ships to know which migrations it needs (readiness).

- **Compatible with the previous release.** A deploy migrates before the new app starts, and a
  rollback runs the previous image on the new schema. So a migration may add schema objects
  (tables, columns, indexes, grants), and may drop or rename only an object that the previous
  release's code no longer reads: a destructive change ships one release after the code stops
  using the object.

- **Destructive statements are marked.** A file with `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, `RENAME`, `REVOKE`,
  `DELETE`, a column type change or `SET NOT NULL` carries a line
  `-- jade:contract <bead>` naming the bead that removed the last reader. `pnpm db:check`
  refuses the file without it.

- **One transaction per file.** The runner applies each file in its own transaction together
  with its ledger row; a failure rolls the file back. A statement that cannot run inside a
  transaction is out of scope until one is needed. A file holds no transaction-control
  statement (`BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, `END`, `ABORT`, `START TRANSACTION`, `SAVEPOINT`,
  `RELEASE`): one would commit the file apart from its ledger row. `pnpm db:check` refuses it.

- **Grants to `jade_app` by name.** The app connects as `jade_app` and owns nothing; the owner,
  `jade_owner`, runs migrations. Every new table needs its grants to `jade_app` in the same file.

- Commit the `.sql` file, `manifest.json` and `meta/` (Drizzle Kit's journal and snapshot)
  together. `pnpm db:check` must pass.

Drizzle Kit's `migrate` and
`push` commands are never used.
